name: Chiffon-Wraith
specific_features: Upper atmosphere so thin it appears translucent like chiffon fabric
Ring system composed of captured comet debris
description: Chiffon-Wraith is an unusual gas giant whose upper atmospheric layers are remarkably thin and translucent, allowing observers to see deep into the planet's banded cloud structure in a way that is impossible with most jovian worlds. The effect creates a layered, sheer appearance reminiscent of chiffon fabric draped over the denser cloud bands below. A delicate ring system of captured cometary debris adds to the ethereal quality, catching starlight and creating a faint halo that makes the planet appear to glow from within.

Despite its ghostly beauty, Chiffon-Wraith is a monster of gravitational force, its dense metallic hydrogen core generating a gravity well that has captured twenty-three moons and cleared its orbital neighborhood of debris for millions of kilometers in every direction. The deeper atmospheric layers are zones of crushing pressure and extreme chemistry, where silicate crystals precipitate and fall as glittering rain through layers of superheated hydrogen. The contrast between the planet's delicate appearance and its lethal reality is profound.

Navigation near Chiffon-Wraith requires exceptional care, as the planet's gravitational influence creates complex tidal effects that have claimed several vessels over the decades. The wreckage of the cargo hauler Persistence drifts in a slowly decaying orbit, its hull crumpled by tidal stresses that the crew never saw coming. The planet's translucent upper atmosphere made it appear smaller and less massive than it was, a visual deception that contributed to the miscalculation.

The ring system contains unusually high concentrations of organic compounds, remnants of the comets that were captured and ground down by gravitational forces over millions of years. Some astrochemists believe these compounds include precursors to amino acids, making the rings a natural laboratory for studying prebiotic chemistry. Automated collection stations have been proposed but not yet funded, as the navigational hazards make any sustained operation around Chiffon-Wraith an expensive proposition. The planet drifts on, beautiful and deadly, a ghost dressed in veils of frozen light.
